images.caption: We enjoyed many lassis (yogurt-based drinks, frequently made with fresh fruit) throughout India. On our last day in Jaipur, we decided to try Lassi Wallah, a stand located around the corner from the hotel. We were fairly careful about eating food off the street, but decided the chance to have a lassi served in a disposable terra cotta mug was too good to pass up. We did have to get over the fact that some old guys scooped the lassis by hand out of a much larger terra cotta container with no refrigeration in site. They were delicious.
images.alt: We enjoyed many lassis (yogurt-based drinks, frequently made with fresh fruit) throughout India. Sujet : Jean-Aubry, G. (1882-1950) -- Correspondance
Annotations à l'encre verte probablement de la main de G. images.caption: View of Jaipur city from Nahargarh Fort. – Pink City Jaipur is UNESCO World Heritage site. The walled city of Jaipur, in India’s north-western state of Rajasthan was founded in 1727 by Sawai Jai Singh II. Unlike other cities in the region located in hilly terrain, Jaipur was established on the plain and built according to a grid plan interpreted in the light of Vedic architecture.
images.alt: View of Jaipur city from Nahargarh Fort. – Pink City Jaipur is UNESCO World Heritage site.
